title: Border Patrol Finds 35 People Hidden in Fake Generator Box on Laredo Flatbed
excerpt: U.S. Border Patrol agents found 35 people crammed inside a locked compartment disguised as a generator box on a flatbed trailer in the ranch lands of Laredo, ac
content:
U.S. Border Patrol agents found 35 people crammed inside a locked compartment disguised as a generator box on a flatbed trailer in the ranch lands of Laredo, according to reports published Nov. 17.

Agents spotted a suspicious vehicle towing the flatbed trailer, according to the reports. What looked like an ordinary generator box turned out to be a hollowed-out, concealed compartment holding 35 people.

The driver faces federal human smuggling charges, according to the reports. The 35 people found inside will be processed for deportation, the reports said.

Border Patrol said transporting people in confined, concealed compartments puts lives at risk, and that its agents are highly trained to spot the hidden details and subtle indicators of illicit smuggling methods that others might overlook. “Every detail matters,” the agency said, according to the report.

The agency did not say when the vehicle was found, did not release the driver's name, and did not say what condition the 35 people were in. Webb Watch is treating those details as unconfirmed until the agency releases them. The driver is presumed innocent unless proven guilty in court.

It is the second such discovery in Laredo in less than a week. On Nov. 13, Laredo Sector agents working with a canine team stopped a tractor-trailer and found 33 people in a hidden compartment, according to a separate report. That driver, a U.S. citizen, was arrested and faces federal human smuggling prosecution under 8 U.S.C. § 1324, and the 33 people face illegal-entry charges under 8 U.S.C. § 1325.

The discoveries follow a Nov. 9 announcement by the U.S. Department of Justice that 14 people were charged in connection with a deadly May incident in which migrants were found in a rail-yard container in Laredo, a case Webb Watch previously reported.

Concealed compartments like the generator box are among the most dangerous smuggling methods agents encounter, because the people inside can be trapped with little air, no water and no way to call for help. The back-to-back discoveries show the method is still in active use on Laredo-area roads, and that agents are finding the compartments through the kind of close inspection Border Patrol described in its statement.

Webb Watch will update this story if Border Patrol releases the date of the stop, the driver's identity or the condition of the people found inside.
